record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
record.original_question: Does every planar graph have obstacle number 1?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 11 Does every planar graph have obstacle number 1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An obstacle representation of a simple graph $G=(V,E)$ consists of an injective placement of the vertices of $G$ as points in the plane together with a finite collection of pairwise-disjoint simple polygonal regions ("obstacles") in the plane, none of which contains any vertex point, such that for every pair of distinct vertices $u,v \in V$: the open straight-line segment between the points representing $u$ and $v$ avoids all obstacles if and only if $uv \in E$. The obstacle number of $G$, denoted $\mathrm{obs}(G)$, is the minimum number of obstacles in any obstacle representation of $G$.

Question: Is it true that every planar graph $G$ satisfies $\mathrm{obs}(G) \le 1$?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture has been disproved: Berman, Chappell, Faudree, Gimbel, Hartman, and Williams showed that the icosahedron (and another 10-vertex planar graph) has obstacle number 2, so not every planar graph has obstacle number 1. The broader question of whether the obstacle number of planar graphs is bounded by a constant remains open.

status_evidence.title: Obstacle number of planar graphs | Open Problem Garden
status_evidence.snippet: A lower bound of 2 was recently shown by Berman et al, who showed that the icosahedron (as well as another planar graph with 10 vertices) has obstacle number 2.
status_evidence.claim: There exist planar graphs with obstacle number at least 2, refuting the conjecture that every planar graph has obstacle number 1.

status_evidence.title: Obstacle Numbers of Planar Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Obstacle Numbers of Planar Graphs (Berman et al.)
status_evidence.claim: A planar graph with obstacle number 2 is exhibited.
